edition: Discover — 17 November 2026 · Haunted Places and Hidden Words
intro: A disputed black-triangle report, a haunted pub and a Welsh farmhouse trailer lead into strange worlds on screen and on the page. There is a complete fantasy story to read, an Orthodox discussion of purgatory, poetry and Christian love, plus two gaming deep dives and the Riverlands at war. All picks are from November. Story dates given only by issue retain month precision, and spoilers are flagged.

items.title: Fresh doubts surround declassified FBI report of 'black triangle' UFO
items.summary: A released report describes FBI personnel claiming to have seen a black triangular craft hover above a ridge and accelerate into a canyon. Former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick questions how much the account establishes, particularly when witness credentials carry more weight than physical evidence.
items.why: A Why Files-style case with an official paper trail and a disputed interpretation. The interesting question is what the document records and how far the available evidence lets you go.

items.title: The Tongue That Makes the Mountain Sing
items.summary: A complete 10,208-word fantasy story from Lightspeed’s November issue. A colonial Scribe ventures into mountain country with a local guide, determined to gather its stories. Language, magical writing and the assumptions behind collecting other people’s knowledge shape the journey. Includes references to sexual violence.
items.why: A substantial piece of fiction to read at leisure, with a world revealed through the uneasy relationship between two travellers. The power of words and competing versions of history should suit your taste for layered fantasy.

items.title: How Silent Hill: Townfall's developer created a fictional town that's still real—'It exists. It's there'
items.summary: Fraser Brown interviews Screen Burn’s director and art director about building St. Amelia from Scottish coastal towns, reference photographs and familiar British interiors. Their account shows how ordinary rooms and accurately scaled streets make the horror feel convincing. Contains location and visual spoilers.
items.why: For the craft behind a haunted place, down to wallpaper, shop signs and isolated fishing streets. It connects your appetite for atmospheric horror with the design choices that make exploration unsettling.

items.title: Discovering the Medieval Origins of Purgatory (w/ Dn. Seraphim Richard Rohlin)
items.summary: A 100-minute discussion of the development of purgatory in medieval and Counter-Reformation Catholicism, presented from an Orthodox apologetic perspective. Cassian King and Seraphim Richard Rohlin examine a doctrine whose history and interpretation remain contested across Christian traditions.
items.why: A substantial comparison for your interest in salvation and the afterlife. It offers a different tradition’s account of how a familiar doctrine developed, giving you claims to investigate alongside Catholic sources.
items.source: Ancient Faith / The Orthodox Apologetics Podcast

items.title: Landlord reveals haunted secrets of the Ring O’ Bells, Middleton
items.summary: Gemma Johnson visits a reputedly haunted pub and interviews its landlord about the Sad Cavalier, cellar shadows and tunnel stories. The interview contrasts the venue’s elaborate legends with the comparatively limited disturbances its present custodians describe.
items.why: A fireside haunting with a welcome human perspective. The gap between a building’s accumulated reputation and what the people living with it actually report is part of the mystery.

items.title: Hate Your Neighbor as Yourself?
items.summary: Richard Clements reads the command to love one’s neighbour through Augustine, Josef Pieper and the idea of willing another person’s good. He argues that healthy self-love and love of others belong together, then considers how resentment and public hostility distort both.
items.why: For your interest in what Christian love actually requires, this gives a philosophical reading of a very familiar commandment. Pieper’s link between love and affirming another person’s existence is especially worth considering.

items.title: Queen’s Domain
items.summary: Ben Love reviews a first-person dungeon crawler inspired by King’s Field, examining its interconnected island, weapon progression and rewarding secrets. The review weighs the pleasure of risky exploration against rougher combat and presentation. Contains setting and exploration spoilers.
items.why: A modern route into the strange, solitary feel of early FromSoftware games. It looks particularly suited to enjoying an unfamiliar fantasy world by discovering its geography and hidden paths yourself.

items.title: "Unsettling" BBC mystery drama set in the Welsh countryside of the '80s lands first-look trailer
items.summary: A preview of Danny Robins’s four-part adaptation of The Witch Farm, with its first trailer. A family’s move to an isolated Welsh farmhouse becomes a story of disturbances, buried history and strained trust. The drama draws on reported experiences and launches on 22 November.
items.why: A new supernatural story to follow if you enjoy witness-led mysteries and haunted-house investigations. The trailer is available now, with the full drama still to come.

items.title: ‘To Be More with Him’: The Poetry of John Paul II
items.summary: Lindsey Weishar introduces Karol Wojtyła’s poetry and theatre, including his use of pen names and his habit of circling an idea through several voices. The essay considers how literature and performance opened a different way into his theology and understanding of human love.
items.why: A quieter reading discovery alongside the mysteries. It introduces a saint through his creative work, with poems and plays to pursue if you enjoy theology expressed through imagery and story.

items.category: A Song of Ice and Fire lore
items.title: Dance Battles of the Riverlands
items.summary: History of Westeros follows the Dance of the Dragons from the perspective of Riverlands nobles, knights and common people, as dragons and rival armies converge on the region. Major Fire & Blood spoilers, including events beyond House of the Dragon’s current adaptation.
items.why: A detailed Westeros-history session focused on the people caught between the great powers. It should appeal to the side of your lore interest that asks how a war looks from the ground.
